economy.summary: As the incumbent, introduced a resolution (HR 357) in September 2025 to create a Pennsylvania Hunger Task Force, citing rising food prices and federal SNAP changes he said would cost more than 140,000 Pennsylvanians their benefits; his district office also distributes free food weekly through a partner outreach program.
economy.short: Proposes state Hunger Task Force, citing food costs, SNAP cuts.

education.summary: Supports charter schools and school vouchers for low-income students; he was the only House Democrat to vote for a bill creating a private-school voucher program, later changing his vote to no, and has called for increased security measures such as cameras and locking doors in Philadelphia schools.
education.short: Supports charter schools and vouchers; voted for voucher bill, then reversed.

healthcare.summary: Has publicly objected to threats against patients and providers of gender-affirming care at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia; this statement concerned gender-affirming care specifically, and no broader healthcare platform was found in his campaign materials.
healthcare.short: Objected to threats against gender-affirming care patients and providers.

guns.summary: Sponsored 2021 legislation (HB 1587) to set mandatory minimum sentences for people with prior records convicted of gun offenses and to allow pretrial detention without bail in some cases, citing Philadelphia's gun violence; he later asked House leaders to put the bill on hold after criticism.
guns.short: Sponsored bill setting mandatory minimums for repeat gun offenses; later paused.
